name: Photorealism
visualIdentity: A credible, lifelike appearance built from plausible scale, surface roughness, contact shadows, reflections, lighting and depth of field. Give objects weight and consistent contact; measured camera moves keep the subject readable. This describes appearance, not proof of filmed footage.
suitableUses: Explicitly suited to product hero shots and material studies. Also fits product launches, premium product pages, engineering explainers and technical training, especially when overlays explain measured details the image cannot. These use cases are stated or inferred from the suggested combinations.
limitations: Avoid unexplained highlights, floating geometry, intersections, excessive blur and implausible acceleration. Keep annotated regions sharp. Photorealistic appearance does not establish physical production or validated physics. The source defines no intrinsic palette; resolve subject colors from references.
palette: Preserve task, brand, reference and asset colors. Optional tokens for new presentation elements only: background #F0EDE5, foreground #2B302F, accent #827D6D; no gradients. The accent is decorative and fails the stated normal-text contrast target (3.517); use the main background/foreground pair (11.458) for candidate text, then check actual compositing. Do not recolor photographed subjects or materials.
motionAndInteraction: Use plausible acceleration, consistent contact and restrained camera motion. Suggested hybrids use slow dolly/orbit moves with holds. Scroll-driven chapters and storytelling can become timed, seekable scenes in video; HTML may map finite scroll progress to reversible states. Dolly needs real depth or a disclosed 2.5D approximation; cursor orbit needs real 3D, fixed target and bounded camera movement, with keyboard/touch and reduced-motion alternatives. Gallery motion requires actual images and captions.
audio: No fixed soundtrack or mandatory layer is specified. Choose music, voiceover, vocals, effects, ambience or silence for the subject and audience, honoring supplied audio requirements. Keep speech intelligible, avoid clipping or competing vocals, and synchronize sound with picture.
assetRequirements: Create PBR models/materials, lights, cameras and keyframed motion in Blender; bake simulations and inspect denoising for lost detail or temporal instability. Cycles is path-traced; EEVEE is a faster real-time-style option. Overlays need verified values anchored to tracked/projected geometry. Galleries need actual images and captions. Supply authorized assets; availability is unspecified.
combinations: Use alone when plausible light and contact tell the story. Pair with style-097 for verified data callouts or style-096 for restrained type and pacing; keep renders dominant and overlays thin. Optional chapter/story patterns fit meaningful progression. Avoid incompatible transitions, unsupported depth, or patterns without relevant scenes. Combinations are suggestions, not requirements.
productionApproach: Blender/Python bpy owns visual construction and motion; Cycles or EEVEE renders. HyperFrames is the primary composition, timing, synchronization, validation and export pipeline; use Remotion only if unavailable or a verified limitation blocks a required capability, recording the reason. Keep rendering and motion style-specific, deterministic and seekable; inspect decoded frames and the full video. Interactive scroll/pointer behavior belongs to HTML delivery.
